items.title: George "Pops" Foster and Mugsy Spanier Interview, 1957-04-21
items.q: The first time I met Bruno Stoyle, he was playing on a tin trombone.

ctx.x: Two trumpets. Trombone. Clarinet. Clarinet. Drums. Bass. Drums and piano. No bass. Soft, man. And then two trumpets. You imagine a drummer. You imagine a drummer. You imagine a drummer. You blow your roof off. It was soft. You could hear. Joe used to put a handkerchief over his fingers, you know, so that Louie wouldn't know what guy

would break he was going to play. They had their breaks numbered, you know. Oh, yeah? Joe would tell them number two break. They'd go play together. Huh? They had their breaks numbered? Oh, sure. Is that so? I thought that Joe thought if he watched his fingers he'd be able to copy it. He never dreamed that you could hear it, you know. Oh, it was really funny those days. Yeah. It was really interesting, yeah. The first time I met Bruno Stoyle, he was playing on a tin trombone. One of those old nickel plate things.…
I know you had an old tin vowel, man. I know that baby little dad was all tied up with some strings holding together.
